items.title: Rudy Van Gelder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Way back in the Prestige days, you know, with Philly Joe and all the people around on that. I used to do little bits with some comedians jokes, or punch lines, things like that.

ctx.x: You have a very highly developed sense of humor, which is a sort of secret. Except during this more relaxed fashion, in the old days, did you used to play funny things for the musicians?

Oh yeah. That was early on, I used to do that. Way back in the Prestige days, you know, with Philly Joe and all the people around on that. I used to do little bits with some comedians jokes, or punch lines, things like that. At the end of a take I’d play it back, and I didn’t have headphones so everybody could hear and there were some funny situations created by that. They were icebreakers, and everybody felt better.
